newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa ends off highs, March AAs dominate.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa ends off highs, March AAs dominate.

text.p: Nearby LIFFE cocoa futures ended with pared gains in another lacklustre session dominated by against actuals (AA) and crosses.
Traders said the most-active March saw some sizable 3,000 lots of AAs by one large commodity house.
"He bought and sold 3,000 lots of March. He's swapping out against physicals and we're not sure why," said one trader.
Overall volume on the exchange reached 6,149 lots, including 800 lots crossed on March 1997/March 1998 which saw deals at between 65 and 69 stg.
Of this, 500 lots were crossed at 65 stg, traders said.
By the close, benchmark December was seven stg higher at 990 stg a tonne after touching the day's high of 993. Other positions were one to nine stg firmer.
Traders also noted some follow-through arbitrage selling in London against New York, prompted by the lower U.S. dollar against the British pound.
U.S. brokerage Merrill Lynch said a cocoa supply deficit in the coming season still seemed a possibility even though the actual crop size remained uncertain.
"...This should restrict the market's downside, at least for the time being," the Merrill Lynch said in its latest Commodity Market Trends report, although it did not quote figures.
A recent spate of supply forecasts put the 1996/97 (Oct-Sept) cocoa deficit at a wide range of between 150,000 and 225,000 tonnes.
Merrill added that good prospects for cocoa demand could keep the market from dropping much further.
